titleEn: What makes food ‘organic’? For many consumers, the answer isn’t always on the label
titleZh: 食品怎样才算“有机”？消费者的理解未必都写在标签上
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: “Organic” is a word we encounter every time we visit the supermarket. It’s also one that can mean very different things to different people.
paragraphs.zh: “有机”是我们每次逛超市都会遇到的一个词，它对不同的人有着不同的含义。

paragraphs.en: Surveys show that taste, quality, environmental concerns and perceived health and safety benefits all influence consumers’ decisions to buy organic food. But less is known about how people interpret “organic” and incorporate it into their everyday lives.
paragraphs.zh: 调查显示，口味、质量、环境问题以及对健康和安全的感知都会影响消费者购买有机食品的决定。但人们如何理解“有机”并将其融入日常生活却知之甚少。

paragraphs.en: Drawing on videos recorded by consumers themselves, my new research explores how these ideas influence people’s relationships with food.
paragraphs.zh: 根据消费者自己录制的视频，我的新研究探讨了这些想法如何影响人们与食物的关系。

paragraphs.en: It shows how the search for food they can trust can lead shoppers from supermarkets to growers and their own gardens, with important lessons for producers, retailers and researchers.
paragraphs.zh: 它展示了寻找他们可以信任的食物如何将购物者从超市引导到种植者和他们自己的花园，为生产商，零售商和研究人员提供了重要的教训。

paragraphs.en: Looking past the organic label
paragraphs.zh: 看过有机标签

paragraphs.en: As in other countries, organic food in New Zealand is big business. Organics Aotearoa New Zealand’s 2025 market report showed the national organic sector to be worth NZ$1.18 billion in 2024.
paragraphs.zh: 与其他国家一样，新西兰的有机食品也是一项大生意。Organics Aotearoa New Zealand的2025年市场报告显示，2024年全国有机食品行业的价值将达到11.8亿新西兰元。

paragraphs.en: While a 2020 government-led consumer survey found price was a barrier for most respondents who didn’t buy organic products, around three-quarters of all respondents still reported buying organic food or drink. So, what exactly are they paying for?
paragraphs.zh: 虽然2020年政府主导的消费者调查发现，价格是大多数不购买有机产品的受访者的障碍，但仍有约四分之三的受访者表示购买了有机食品或饮料。那么，他们到底在为什么付钱呢？

paragraphs.en: Organic agriculture is generally understood as a system that supports the health of soils, ecosystems and people. Certification helps ensure organic products meet recognised standards throughout the supply chain.
paragraphs.zh: 有机农业通常被理解为支持土壤、生态系统和人类健康的系统。认证有助于确保有机产品在整个供应链中符合公认的标准。

paragraphs.en: Yet my research highlighted that consumers don’t necessarily define organic food by what’s on the label.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，我的研究强调，消费者不一定根据标签上的内容来定义有机食品。

paragraphs.en: Across three related studies, I drew on the experiences of 33 Chinese consumers of organic food, examining how trust, personal values and migration experiences shaped their food practices. While not representative of all Chinese or New Zealand consumers, the findings offer insights into how people practise organic living.
paragraphs.zh: 在三项相关研究中，我收集了33名中国有机食品消费者的经验，研究了信任、个人价值观和移民经历如何影响他们的饮食习惯。虽然这些研究结果并不能代表所有中国或新西兰消费者，但它为人们如何实践有机生活提供了见解。

paragraphs.en: During the COVID-19 pandemic, restrictions made it difficult to observe participants’ routines. So I asked participants in one of the studies to record short videos showing their food and how they obtained it.
paragraphs.zh: 在COVID-19大流行期间，限制使得很难观察参与者的日常生活。所以我要求其中一项研究的参与者录制短视频，展示他们的食物以及他们如何获得食物。

paragraphs.en: They could film their groceries, unpack a delivery or take the camera into their garden. I then used their videos to guide interviews, asking why they had chosen to show particular things.
paragraphs.zh: 他们可以拍摄他们的食品杂货，打开包裹或把相机带到他们的花园里。然后我用他们的视频指导采访，问他们为什么选择展示特定的东西。

paragraphs.en: The recordings highlighted how organic consumption could involve growing and sharing food as well as buying it. Some participants showed vegetables growing at home, while others presented produce from a community garden.
paragraphs.zh: 这些录音强调了有机消费如何涉及种植和分享食物以及购买食物。一些参与者展示了家中种植的蔬菜，而其他人则展示了社区花园的农产品。

paragraphs.en: One person filmed her supermarket shopping. After returning to China from studying in the United States, she began buying organic products in Shanghai. Later, she started making tofu, growing bean sprouts and harvesting vegetables on her balcony.
paragraphs.zh: 一个人拍下了她逛超市的场景，从美国留学回国后，她开始在上海购买有机产品，后来她开始在自家阳台上做豆腐、种豆芽、收蔬菜。

paragraphs.en: Another person unpacked a box of produce, explaining how he’d asked the supplier to pack it tightly and use less plastic to reduce waste. Both examples showed how people’s interest in organic food influenced their everyday habits in ways that simply asking about their shopping might not have uncovered.
paragraphs.zh: 另一个人打开一盒农产品，解释他是如何要求供应商包装紧密，减少塑料使用以减少浪费的。这两个例子都表明，人们对有机食品的兴趣如何影响他们的日常习惯，而这些影响是简单地询问他们的购物情况可能无法发现的。

paragraphs.en: The videos also challenged some assumptions. One participant described himself as an enthusiastic organic consumer but showed expensive supermarket products without organic labels.
paragraphs.zh: 这些视频也挑战了一些假设。一位参与者称自己是一个热情的有机消费者，但展示的是没有有机标签的昂贵超市产品。

paragraphs.en: Further discussion revealed that he’d linked organic food with premium prices, luxury packaging and upmarket shops, rather than certification or production methods. His understanding differed markedly from the researchers’ definition of organic food.
paragraphs.zh: 进一步的讨论表明，他将有机食品与高价、豪华包装和高档商店联系在一起，而不是与认证或生产方法联系在一起。他的理解与研究人员对有机食品的定义明显不同。

paragraphs.en: The videos were selective accounts of everyday life, with participants deciding what to show. But examining those choices alongside interviews helped explain why particular products and activities felt important to them.
paragraphs.zh: 这些视频是对日常生活的选择性描述，由参与者决定播放什么。但在采访的同时审视这些选择有助于解释为什么特定的产品和活动对他们来说很重要。

paragraphs.en: Why trust is key
paragraphs.zh: 为什么信任是关键

paragraphs.en: Trust emerged as a central theme across my research – and it’s also a concern for shoppers more generally. In the 2020 survey, for instance, 21% of New Zealand respondents who didn’t buy organic products cited a lack of trust in organic claims as a barrier.
paragraphs.zh: 在我的研究中，信任是一个中心主题，也是购物者普遍关心的问题。例如，在2020年的调查中，21%没有购买有机产品的新西兰受访者表示，对有机产品的宣传缺乏信任是一个障碍。

paragraphs.en: While certain participants in my research relied on certification, others placed greater faith in personal recommendations, community networks or direct relationships with growers.
paragraphs.zh: 虽然我的研究中的某些参与者依赖于认证，但其他人更相信个人推荐，社区网络或与种植者的直接关系。

paragraphs.en: Doubts about conventional food systems sometimes extended to organic claims, prompting people to change their food sources or grow and prepare more themselves. Consumers could share a desire for trustworthy food while holding very different ideas about what made it trustworthy.
paragraphs.zh: 对传统食品体系的怀疑有时会延伸到有机食品，促使人们改变食物来源，或者自己种植和准备更多的食物。消费者可能对值得信赖的食品有着共同的渴望，但对什么让它值得信赖却有着截然不同的想法。

paragraphs.en: For producers and retailers, the findings reinforce the need for clear information about where organic food comes from, how it is produced and how its claims are verified. For researchers, they demonstrate the value of videos and interviews in exploring consumers’ habits and attitudes beyond their purchasing decisions.
paragraphs.zh: 对于生产商和零售商来说，这些发现加强了对有机食品来自哪里、如何生产以及如何验证其声明的明确信息的需求。对于研究人员来说，他们展示了视频和访谈在探索消费者购买决策之外的习惯和态度方面的价值。

paragraphs.en: Someone who grows more of their own food might buy less from an organic retailer, all while becoming more committed to the values they associate with organic living.
paragraphs.zh: 那些自己种植更多食物的人可能会从有机零售商那里购买更少的东西，同时更加致力于他们与有机生活相关的价值观。

paragraphs.en: Ultimately, what people do with food, what they value and whom they trust can tell us just as much about their choices as what they put in their shopping trolley.
paragraphs.zh: 最终，人们如何处理食物、他们重视什么以及他们信任谁，可以告诉我们他们的选择，就像他们在购物车里放了什么一样。
